idiom_name: new Proxy(service, { get, apply }) forwarding through Reflect
implementation_notes: The language supplies the equivalence mechanism itself: new Proxy(target, handler) intercepts property access and calls through get/apply traps, and Reflect forwards the operation to the target unchanged, so every member of the service client keeps working and the control logic lives in the trap instead of in hand-written forwarders. The interception is in-process and lexical only - a Proxy in front of a network client cannot see another process's traffic - so the wire hop belongs to a Node-core reverse proxy or an out-of-process proxy, and server frameworks express the same idea as middleware (app.use).
pitfalls: Traps must respect the engine's invariants: returning a different value for a non-configurable, non-writable property or on a non-extensible target throws a TypeError.
Returning a fresh wrapper on every get breaks method identity and unbound comparisons (p.fn !== p.fn); memoise per target when identity matters.
A Proxy governs only in-process access: it cannot enforce policy for other clients, other languages or traffic that never flows through this object.

variants.name: Node core reverse proxy (http.createServer + http.request)
variants.implementation_notes: Without any dependency the http module can front an HTTP service: create a server, build the outbound request with http.request, apply policy on the headers, then pipe the request body through and pipe the response back so nothing is buffered. This is the language-agnostic form - other processes and other languages address the proxy, not the service - and it is the shape the middleware ecosystem (Express middleware, http-proxy-middleware) wraps for convenience.
pitfalls: Buffering bodies to inspect them defeats streaming and can exhaust memory under load; keep the piping and inspect headers unless the policy truly needs the payload.
Socket and agent behaviour matters more than the code: without keep-alive agents and upstream timeouts the proxy opens a connection per request and leaks sockets on hangs.
Hop-by-hop headers (connection, transfer-encoding, upgrade) must not be forwarded verbatim, and websockets need an upgrade handler instead of the plain request path.
